note: Daily council 2026-08-06. Named to sort last in this directory (newest_request() is lexicographic, not mtime — 2026-08-05 defect, propose-only, unfixed at session open) and checked against analytics/fetch-results/ for a name collision before firing. FOUR QUESTIONS. (1+2) A/81/17 watch, day 6 of the publication window, at the Commission Sessions posting location, in the standard same-page positive-control form: the target symbol plus a control string known present on that page (A/80/17). The undocs.org / docs.un.org symbol route stays RETIRED (2026-08-04) as carrying no existence information at the relay's reduction level. Relay nulls are about RENDERED TEXT: fetch_relay.py strips attributes, so a symbol appearing only inside an href is invisible to this channel. (3) B7 DISCHARGE CONTROL, pre-registered here before any result exists. Question: is the page title 'China - Switzerland BIT (2009)' that the relay retrieved for treaty 978 keyed to the numeric database id, or merely an inverse of the slug we ourselves typed? Method: request the same numeric id 978 under a deliberately false slug. DECISION RULE, FIXED IN ADVANCE — (a) HTTP 200 and the excerpt head still reads 'China - Switzerland BIT (2009)': the title is keyed to the id, the slug is not load-bearing, and B7 discharges to database-record level; (b) HTTP 200 and the head reads a title derived from 'zzz---zzz-bit-1900-': the title is slug-derived, it identifies nothing, and B7 STANDS IN FULL — every 978 retrieval in the record is identified at URL-slug level only; (c) 404, or a final_url differing from the requested URL: the id alone does not resolve or is rewritten, the retrieval cannot be separated from the slug supplied, and B7 STANDS. Branches (b) and (c) are the NEGATIVE result. This row is a control on our own method, not a discovery request. (4+5+6) Huawei Technologies v. Kingdom of Sweden (ICSID ARB/22/2) award watch, against the 2026-07-31 docket baseline read from this same page: Status of Proceeding 'Pending', Procedural Orders Nos. 1-8 only, and 'Latest Development: July 10, 2025 - Each party files a reply submission on costs.' Row 4 anchors on the literal field label 'Latest Development' and is the content-bearing same-page positive control; row 5 anchors on 'Procedural Order No. 8', a string two seats verified present on 2026-07-31; row 6 probes for 'Procedural Order No. 9', whose absence against a passing control is a null on docket movement and NOT a statement about the award's existence. The case-detail URL is the one already carried in the record (STATE_OF_THE_ANSWER.md:188 and five daily records); this is retrieval of a docket page the record already identified, not discovery.
